verdict.rationale: Secureframe documents automations that run in the background without user action: continuous daily monitoring with alerts for failing tests, automated evidence collection through integrations, and automatic shadow-IT detection. Users can also configure recurring schedules (not just one-off actions) for access reviews and risk-based vendor reviews, plus customized reminders. However, these are fixed, built-in compliance automations rather than user-defined background automations or agents. missing for 10: a general user-configurable automation or workflow builder, user-defined triggers and actions, autonomous AI agents running in the background, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Continuous daily monitoring of your compliance status with alerts for failing tests.
Automate manual evidence collection utilizing our 100+ integrations
Designate reviewers per system and use recurring schedules, reminders, and status indicators to keep the process moving.
Users can also set up recurring reviews based on risk level, and set up tasks and notifications via Jira and Slack.
Customize notifications for required regular tasks throughout the year including quarterly user access reviews and annual penetration testing.
Secureframe helps uncover shadow IT by automatically detecting apps accessed by employees via SSO
